One complete worked example

One burst. Four timestamps.
A position you can trace.

A 10 km square, a UE at (4, 3) km and 100 ps pairwise clock RMS. Follow every assumption through to the numerical result.

The setupArrival timesTiming budgetPosition uncertaintyMonte Carlo checkWhat it means

Specify the experiment.

Place anchors at (0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 10) and (0, 10) km, each 30 m high. The UE height is known at 1.5 m, so its vertical separation is 28.5 m. One identifiable uplink burst reaches all four receivers. Their unknown common transmission epoch cancels when arrival times are differenced.

ri = √[(x − xi)² + (y − yi)² + 28.5²]Coordinates and ranges are in metres. The mean atmospheric delay is assumed corrected before fitting.

The clock assumption is 100 ps RMS difference between two BS clocks. Independent per-anchor residuals are therefore 100 / √2 = 70.71 ps, plus any common reference error that the position fit absorbs.

Calculate the four arrivals.

AnchorRange, mGeometric flight time, µsTDoA versus BS1, µs

The ideal range differences identify (4,000, 3,000) m. In a real receiver, each timestamp also contains clock, RF-chain, propagation and signal-estimation errors.

ti = t0 + ri/c + bi + di + ai + ni

Give every link its own noise.

Assume a 100 MHz flat baseband spectrum and 20 dB observation energy SNR at 10 km. With free-space distance scaling, the closer receivers get higher pilot energy SNR. A 100 ps receiver implementation term is added beyond the thermal lower bound.

AnchorPilot energy SNRThermal ToA boundClock RMS

Add 100 ps independent RF calibration uncertainty, 50 ps independent path residual, 1 cm isotropic anchor-coordinate uncertainty and one common residual refractivity uncertainty of 1 N-unit. The last term is correlated across links; it is kept as a rank-one covariance term rather than added as independent noise.

Why the old maps looked alike: identical per-anchor error budgets give C(x, y) = σ²G(x, y). Changing only σ rescales the same map. Here both per-link SNR and correlated propagation terms are modeled explicitly. Distinct shapes follow from assumptions, not from changing the colours.

Propagate the full covariance.

Joint generalized least squares fits horizontal position and an unknown emission epoch. It uses the full observation covariance, including shared propagation uncertainty. Differencing all observations against BS1 gives an equivalent answer only when the reference-timestamp correlations are retained.

Cxy = [(HᵀR−1H)−1]1:2,1:2H has two horizontal range derivatives and a column of ones for emission distance.
Predicted horizontal RMS9.76 cm
Predicted radial R9516.97 cm
Clock-only contribution2.16 cm

These are conditional single-fix predictions under this model, not a hardware accuracy specification.

Check it with noisy timestamps.

The offline check generates 12,000 nonlinear localization trials for this position and each clock setting. Clock, calibration, survey and atmospheric offsets are drawn once per trial; receiver noise is fresh. The solver starts from a noisy-data coarse search, never from the true UE position, and its final coordinates are not clipped to the square.

Pairwise clock RMSPredicted RMSSimulated RMSSimulated radial R95

At 100 ps, the nonlinear simulation agrees with the local covariance. A 1 ns clock increases error, even with the identical radio and calibration model. Exact values vary slightly with Monte Carlo sampling.

Recreate and change this example

Keep the conclusion proportionate.

Under this chosen 10 km model, roughly 10 cm horizontal RMS is plausible in the calculation. The model cannot establish site-wide radio availability, real multipath rejection, detector performance or a commercial guarantee. Those require an RF calibration experiment and an independently surveyed field trial.

Averaging many bursts reduces independent receiver noise. It does not remove a fixed clock offset, a calibration bias or a persistent path delay. The explorer’s “one fixed installation” mode makes this distinction visible.

Qelora

A proposed timing and key platform for precise, accountable radio positioning. Numerical results are conditional simulations, not field specifications.
